topic: Unlocking the Riemann Zeta Function: The Bridge Between Numbers and Geometry
target_audience: University students (STEM) and advanced mathematics enthusiasts

sections.title: The Mystery of Primes: Meet the Detective
lecture_lines: Prime numbers appear scattered and random across the field.
Meet Detective Prime, searching for patterns in their distribution.
The Riemann zeta function reveals their hidden, secret map.
animations: A scattered field of white dots (#FFFFFF) representing prime numbers (2, 3, 5, 7, 11...) appears on a black background.
An icon of 'Detective Prime' enters from the left, scanning the scattered dots with a magnifying glass.
The scattered dots shift and align into a perfectly ordered grid as the gold formula ζ(s) (#FFD700) fades in above them.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Power of Infinite Sums
lecture_lines: Infinite steps can lead to a finite, definite distance.
Imagine walking halfway to a destination every single second.
Some series converge, while the harmonic series grows forever.
animations: A number line from 0 to 2 appears; a walker moves in increments of 1, 1/2, 1/4, 1/8, getting closer to 2.
The equation 1 + 1/2 + 1/4 + 1/8 +... = 2 appears in light blue (#ADD8E6) above the number line.
The Harmonic series 1 + 1/2 + 1/3 + 1/4 +... appears in red (#FF4500), with an arrow pointing off-screen to infinity.

sections.title: Defining the Zeta Function
lecture_lines: The zeta function sums one over n to power s.
At s equals one, the harmonic series explodes infinitely.
As s increases, the sum settles into finite values.
For s equals two, we solve the famous Basel Problem.
The function converges for all values greater than one.
animations: The formal definition ζ(s) = ∑ (1/n^s) for n=1 to ∞ appears in the center in white (#FFFFFF).
A slider for 's' appears; as 's' moves to 1, the terms 1/1, 1/2, 1/3... stack vertically into a tower that grows off-screen.
As 's' moves to 2, the terms 1/1, 1/4, 1/9... appear as shrinking squares on a balance scale that remains level.
The specific solution ζ(2) = π²/6 is highlighted in gold (#FFD700) next to the balance scale.
A box labeled 'Convergence: s > 1' appears in green (#90EE90) to define the function's initial domain.

sections.title: The Euler Product: The Prime Connection
lecture_lines: The zeta function transforms into a product over primes.
Animated gears represent primes building every single natural number.
This bridge links basic counting to the depth of primes.
animations: The Zeta sum on the left and the Euler Product (∏ 1/(1-p^-s)) on the right appear, connected by a large equal sign.
Animated 'Prime Gears' labeled 2, 3, 5, 7... begin to rotate in sync.
Natural numbers (1, 2, 3, 4...) flow out from the spinning prime gears like products from a factory line.

sections.title: Entering the Complex Realm (Analytic Continuation)
lecture_lines: We extend the function into the infinite complex plane.
Shading marks the initial region where the sum converges.
Analytic continuation expands the function's reach across the map.
Visualize magnitudes as mountains and valleys in this landscape.
A single point at s equals one remains undefined.
animations: A 2D complex plane appears with the horizontal axis σ and vertical axis 'it'.
The region where σ > 1 is shaded in light blue (#ADD8E6) to show the initial domain.
The plane is filled with a heat map where color intensity represents the magnitude |ζ(s)|.
A semi-transparent layer representing analytic continuation expands to cover the full plane.
A bright white (#FFFFFF) glowing point appears at s = 1 to mark the function's pole.

sections.title: The Riemann Hypothesis: The Critical Line
lecture_lines: We focus on the critical strip between zero and one.
A yellow line marks exactly one half on the axis.
Riemann conjectured all non-trivial zeros lie on this line.
Like a tightrope walker, the function maintains perfect balance.
Proving this hypothesis would unlock the secret of primes.
animations: The view zooms into the 'Critical Strip' between σ=0 and σ=1, highlighted in grey (#808080).
A bright yellow (#FFFF00) vertical line is drawn at σ = 0.5, labeled as the 'Critical Line'.
A sequence of blue dots (#0000FF) representing zeros appears, all perfectly aligned on the yellow line.
A tightrope walker icon moves along the yellow line, successfully crossing the gap between the zeros.
The text 'Riemann Hypothesis' appears in bold gold (#FFD700) as the walker reaches the other side.

sections.title: Summary and Real-World Impact
lecture_lines: We compress these complex insights into a single core.
This math powers the security of our digital world.
Thus, the music of primes plays in perfect harmony.
animations: A montage of the prime grid, Euler gears, and the critical line shrinks into a central glowing core.
A digital shield icon labeled 'Encryption' appears, powered by energy pulses from the central core.
The screen fades to black with the final text 'The Music of Primes' appearing in soft green (#90EE90).
